extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering data set consisting of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine paired with Wikipedia pages and annotated answers.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions are sampled from real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine, filtered by heuristics, and paired with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine and Wikipedia pages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Queries were filtered using simple heuristics to discard non-questions while retaining queries of 8 words or more.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators are presented with a question and a Wikipedia page, and must identify if the question is good, select a long answer (HTML bounding box) if present, and select a short answer (entity/entities or yes/no) within the long answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors analyzed human variability and annotation quality by collecting 25-way annotations on a subset of examples and comparing them with consensus judgments from four experts.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Single annotations for training data, 5-way annotations for development and test data, and 25-way annotations for a small subset.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset relies exclusively on Wikipedia for factual information, which may introduce biases.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating open-domain question answering systems.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions (NQ), a new data set for QA research

description.evidence: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set. Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. [...] We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. [...] We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream. [...] The goal of these heuristics is to discard a large proportion of queries that are non-questions, while retaining the majority of queries of 8 words or more in length that are questions.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: An annotator is presented with a (question, Wikipedia page) pair. The annotator retums a (long answer, short answer) pair. The long answer (l) can be an HTML bounding box on the Wikipedia page [...] The short answer (s) can be a span or set of spans (typically entities) within l that answer the question, a boolean yes or no answer, or NULL.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We also describe analysis of 25-way annotations on 302 examples, giving insights into human variability on the annotation task.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Part of speech tags and entities are identified using Google’s Cloud NLP API

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We focus on Wikipedia as it is a very important source of factual information, and we believe that stylistically it is similar to other sources of factual information on the Web; however, like any data set there may be biases in this choice.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: Our goals are three-fold: 1) To provide large-scale end-to-end training data for the QA problem. 2) To provide a data set that drives research in natural language understanding.
